newsitem.title: UK: S&P predicts record offshore drilling earnings.
newsitem.headline: S&P predicts record offshore drilling earnings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's on Wednesday forecast offshore drilling industry earnings and cash flows would reach record levels in the next few years.

The latest issue of the S&P publication CreditWeek said industry players should "feel broad-based financial improvements in the near term" due to a major recovery led by declining costs for oil and gas exploration and development.

"For instance, Noble Drilling (BB plus), Global Marine (BB minus), and Reading & Bates (BB minus) have all recently seen rating upgrades and Falcon Drilling's outlook has been revised to positive from stable (B plus)," S&P said.
"While the offshore drilling industry's credit quality has improved, large-scale rating upgrades are still constrained by the industry's volatility," said S&P analysts Carlos Catoya and Joy Magtoto.
"Nevertheless, modest upgrades could occur in cases where fiscal prudence and market rationalisation serve to bolster a company's business position."
S&P said the industry's current turnaround, unlike past economic recoveries, was not prompted by higher oil or gas prices.
Instead, the recovery stemmed from cost reductions in oil and natural gas reserve finding-and-development.
At the same time, rising energy commodity prices, tightening availability of some drilling rig types, and expiring deep water leases had also contributed to the industry's healthy recovery.
The recovery's impact had varied between drilling markets due to the unique demand and supply characteristics of each market segment, Catoya and Magtoto said.
S&P said contract drillers with asset-type diversity, and international and deep water-depth capabilities, should benefit most from the recovery.
